audit.why: Packet carries 53.96% over 404 games and the win-rate table matches. No change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content-layer level chart hands Quinn 6 of 7 stages while the data says Rumble wins the lane 53.96%. The full layer's phases already read Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Rumble, so the two layers also contradict each other.
audit.why: Quinn only owns level 1, where Blinding Assault's 1025 range beats Flamespitter's 600 cone. From level 2 onward Rumble's damage is unaffected by her single defensive tool and she has to enter his cone to use Vault at all.
audit.corrected: Chart reads Quinn / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer notes that Quinn's Blinding Assault blind does not reduce Rumble's damage. Worse, dontsFull[0] and report[11] both list 'Fight into her blind' as a mistake, actively telling the player to give up his best window.
audit.why: Blind in League causes basic attacks to miss. Rumble's entire damage output is abilities — Flamespitter (Q), Electro Harpoon (E) and The Equalizer (R). Quinn's primary defensive cooldown against melee toplaners is close to dead weight in this matchup, and that is the single biggest reason a melee-range champion posts 54% into a marksman.
audit.corrected: Blind stops basic attacks only. When Quinn spends Blinding Assault, walk in and run the full Flamespitter cone — she has just used her escape button for nothing.
sources: League Wiki: Blind affects basic attacks only

audit.whatIsWrong: The text treats Vault purely as an escape ('vault your Flamespitter engage', 'vault out'). It never states that Vault dashes Quinn onto Rumble before it bounces her away.
audit.why: Vault dashes to the enemy, then leaps off the target and lands near Quinn's maximum attack range. The dash-in half puts her inside the 600-unit Flamespitter cone at point-blank range. Holding Q until she commits Vault converts her escape into a free full-cone trade.
audit.corrected: Hold Flamespitter until Vault lands her next to you — the dash brings her inside the cone before it throws her back out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json (E: 'dashes to an enemy... Upon reaching the target, she leaps off')

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is described only as a slow ('kill Quinn's movement speed'). Its magic-resist reduction, and the fact Rumble carries two charges, is never used.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist on hit and Rumble holds 2 harpoons. Landing both before Flamespitter or The Equalizer means the cone and the ult both land into stacked shred. That is a concrete cast order, not a preference.
audit.corrected: Both harpoons first, cone second — each harpoon cuts her magic resist, so Flamespitter lands on a shredded target.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (E: 'reducing their Magic Resist... Rumble can carry 2 harpoons')

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat Behind Enemy Lines as an unanswerable roam ('outpaces your roam threat', 'before your Equalizer can answer'). Rumble has a direct counter that is never mentioned.
audit.why: Behind Enemy Lines needs a take-off before Quinn flies, and champion damage interrupts it. Electro Harpoon reaches 850 units and The Equalizer leaves burning ground that keeps applying champion damage. Either one stops the roam at source rather than chasing it.
audit.corrected: Hold a harpoon charge when she starts shoving — one hit from 850 range cancels the Behind Enemy Lines take-off and pins her in lane.
sources: League Wiki: Behind Enemy Lines is interrupted by champion damage

audit.whatIsWrong: Vault is repeatedly called 'matchup-defining' and the player is told to 'track it', but no number is ever given.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8 seconds. Flamespitter is 10/9/8/7/6. Early on Rumble's cone comes back faster than her escape, which is the mechanical reason the trade pattern works from level 2. Without the numbers 'track Vault' is unusable advice.
audit.corrected: Vault is 12s at rank 1 and still 10s at rank 3, against a 10-to-8s Flamespitter — your cone recycles faster than her exit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flamespitter is called a 'channel' in five separate places ('before your Flamespitter channel completes', 'the channel deals real damage', etc.).
audit.why: Flamespitter is not a channel. Rumble moves, auto-attacks and casts freely for its full 3-second duration, and nothing Quinn has cancels it. The wording implies Vault's brief interrupt shuts the ability down, which teaches the player to hold Q for a window that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Flamespitter runs for 3 seconds while you walk and auto — Vault only moves Quinn out of the cone, it does not stop the ability.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (Q: 'torches opponents in front of him... for 3 seconds', no channel flag)

edits.before: Quinn beats you from the moment minions meet. Her Harrier passive marks you on the approach and every auto she lands under that mark deals bonus damage — before your Heat reaches Danger Zone she is already winning trades for free. Do not walk forward to farm under her auto range; instead last-hit with Flamespitter at its cone tip and accept chip damage rather than standing still in a passive-mark trade you will lose. Your only early agency is double Electro-Harpoon: if she oversteps to run up a Harrier auto, hit her with the first harpoon, bait the vault, then land the second as she lands — that is the only combo she cannot easily sidestep at this stage. Do not let her bully you into Overheat; silence with no Scrap Shield up is a free punish window for her.
edits.after: Quinn pokes you out of the first two levels: Harrier marks you on the approach and Blinding Assault reaches 1025 units, well outside Flamespitter's 600 cone. Take the chip and farm — the blind itself is the tell that she has misread the matchup, because it only stops basic attacks and every point of Rumble damage comes from an ability. From level 2 your pattern beats hers. Both Electro Harpoons first: each one cuts her magic resist and slows her, and only then turn on Flamespitter, which is not a channel — you walk and auto through its full three seconds. Vault is the mistake you are waiting for, because it dashes her onto you before it throws her back, and that instant inside the cone at Danger Zone heat is most of her health bar.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are when Quinn locks in her pattern: shove, poke a Harrier auto, vault your Flamespitter engage, shove again. Your Scrap Shield is her primary tracking target — she will never commit while it is up, and the moment it expires she will re-engage. Use the threat of Equalizer to make her respect dragon-side positioning: she cannot freely walk into the river if a burning wall can cut off her retreat. At 6 she immediately gains global mobility that outpaces your roam threat unless you have Equalizer ready — shove and ping her position the moment she leaves lane, and if you cannot Equalize her roam yourself, wave-clear and take plates while she is gone rather than chasing a lost skirmish.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are decided by Vault's cooldown — 12 seconds at rank 1, still 10 at rank 3, against a Flamespitter that returns in 8. While it is up, hold your harpoons and farm with the cone tip; the moment she spends it, run the full chain and she has no exit. Keep the wave nearer your tower so she has to step inside 600 units to contest it. At 6 she gains Behind Enemy Lines, but champion damage interrupts the take-off: one Electro Harpoon from 850 range cancels the roam outright, so hold a charge whenever she starts shoving. If she does get out, do not chase — shove in, take the plate, and let Equalizer answer the roam on the map instead.

edits.before: Two items in and Quinn's kite pattern is at full power, but your Equalizer finally becomes the matchup-defining tool in the other direction. Group with your team and force fights in tight corridors — the Rift Herald choke, baron pit, or dragon circle — where a well-placed Equalizer traps her and her team in the burning wall regardless of vault range. Quinn's roaming strength is your greatest late threat: keep your ult off cooldown and call her position every time she leaves the minimap, because a 3000-gold swing on the opposite side of the map outweighs anything you can do in the 1v1 you are losing anyway. You cannot beat her in the side lane at this stage; your job is to make your global presence more impactful than hers.
edits.after: Two items in, this stops being a poke lane and becomes a corridor problem. Equalizer laid across the Baron choke, the dragon pit mouth or a jungle entrance does two things Quinn cannot answer: the slow outlasts Vault's 675-unit hop, and the ticking champion damage interrupts Behind Enemy Lines every time she tries to take off inside it. Keep the ult up whenever she is missing from the minimap and call her position, because her roam is still worth more than anything either of you does in a side lane. In grouped fights she must walk into your cone to collect Harrier resets — bank both harpoons on her before the fight opens so the magic-resist shred is already up when Equalizer lands.

notes: Level chart: the content win[] array gave Quinn 6 of 7 stages against a 53.96% Rumble win rate. The correct chart is Quinn / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble. The full layer's phases[] already held that shape apart from stage 1, which I corrected. I could NOT correct content win[1], win[2] and win[5] from 'Quinn' to 'Rumble' because that is 5 -> 6 characters, +20%, outside the applier's +/-10% band; I set those three to 'Skill' instead, which at least stops the chart contradicting the data. Please set win[1], win[2] and win[5] to 'Rumble' by hand if you want the two layers identical. Separately, the full layer calls Quinn 'he/him' in several places; I fixed breakdown.mid and report[12].t where I had a substantive edit to make anyway, but dosFull[1].d, report[9].t and breakdown.late still say 'he'.
